4.43.betting_forecast: 7/4 Ancient State, 5/2 Mick's Spirit, 5/1 Spendmore Lane, 6/1 Aleppo Pepper, Lequinto.
4.43.spotlight_verdict: Ancient State still has more to come as a sprinter and he isn't opposed lightly but MICK'S SPIRIT (nap) is a hard horse to pass around here when able to dominate and that may be the case today.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: One promising run in Ireland in January 2025; she was returning from 435 days when a modest third of five in a Southwell maiden 19 days ago; not solid now handicapping.
3-3 over 5f, including here, and he took his form to a new level with a comfortable Southwell success last month; up 6lb and now tackles Class 5 company but his ceiling is yet to be established.
horses.breeding: b g Dandy Man - No More Thrills

horses.spotlight_comment: No AW win since December 2021 but there have been some good runs on both Polytrack and Tapeta this year, including C&D, and yesterday's 6f second was another sound display; wasn't helping his rider under pressure on that occasion and opposable for win purposes.
Prolific C&D winner, most recently when making all 54 days ago; a 3lb rise won't stop him if in the same form and he may not have to work too hard to lead; major player.

Two 5f wins this year, making all at Wolverhampton on the second occasion off a 9lb lower mark; her ability to overcome this mark isn't in question but the start continues to be an issue and others look safer.

5.18.betting_forecast: 9/4 Get This In, 3/1 Champion Lawman, 5/1 Rogue Defence, 6/1 Scheffler, 8/1 Roi De Coeur, 16/1 Annahita, Kennington, 20/1
5.18.spotlight_verdict: Those with experience don't set a daunting standard and it would be no surprise to see a newcomer go well. Rogue Defence and Champion Lawman (second choice) look the likeliest types from that category but GET THIS IN showed enough at two to think he had a future and he could prove a different proposition over 1m+ this year.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Kept on for a never-dangerous seventh of 13 at Kempton in November (1m); open to improvement this year but such progress is a must.

44,000euros yearling; seventh foal; brother to 7f-8.5f winner Panama Red (including 2yo/Listed/US; RPR 102), half-brother to three winners including Power Of States (1m-11.5f including 2yo/AW; 106) and Key Witness (7f/1m including AW; 88); dam maiden (83); enough paper appeal to warrant a second look.

Showed clear signs of ability in two 7f runs as a 2yo, beaten 3l into sixth at Kempton when last seen 188 days ago; gelded since then; bred to appreciate the longer trip; open to considerable improvement this year.

22,000gns yearling; third foal; half-brother to 8.6f AW/1m2f turf winner Dashinwhitesargent (RPR 82); dam 7f/1m winner (100), half-sister to useful winners Showout (6f 2yo Listed) and Landwade Lad (1m2f/1m3f); one of three runners for the stable.
Modest form in two runs over shorter last summer; absent 267 days and the step up in trip isn't enough to tempt.
Big prices and poor form in two bumpers this spring; hard to recommend.
Unplaced in two 1m maidens at Kempton this spring; unlikely to come into his own until tackling middle-distance handicaps.

16,000gns yearling, resold 30,000gns yearling; eighth foal; half-brother to winners Meraas (6f including AW/dirt/Group 3; RPR 109), Global Hero (1m turf/8.6f AW; 92) and Winning Point (6f AW; 84); dam 1m Group 3 winner (108); already gelded; starting out in a winnable race and worth a market check.

First foal of an Italian 8.7f/1m1f winner (RPR 92), herself a half-sister to Listed-placed winners Cima Fire (7f 2yo-1m3f) and Giausar (1m2f, placed up to 1m7f); starts out in a winnable race and he needs a market check.

Shaped nicely over 7f here on debut, keeping on well in the closing stages; failed to build on it when last of nine at Wolverhampton 11 days ago (6f); should be more potent over a mile but the widest stall isn't optimal.

Fifth foal; half-brother to winners Wyoming (6f 2yo; RPR 89), Post Rider (1m/8.3f; 83) and Geelong (8.6f-11.4f including 2yo/AW; 76); dam 1m4f winner (including AW; 102); bred to have a bright future but it is likely to be over longer trips than this; stable run three.
Big prices and only minor promise in two fillies' novice events at around 1m this spring; others appeal more for win purposes.

5.50.betting_forecast: 7/2 Rogue Messiah, 4/1 Alasrae, Eternal Solace, 11/2 Comprador, 7/1 Manly Fireball, 8/1 Bone Marra, 12/1 Nifty, 14/1 Merlier,
5.50.spotlight_verdict: This looks competitive. Ollie Sangster's pair Eternal Solace and Bone Marra both have something to recommend them while Akabusi and the thriving Alasrae (second choice) also come right into the reckoning. Comprador will be popular on his handicap debut for a yard in rude health but ROGUE MESSIAH is preferred. He may have faced a tough task trying to give weight to a promising rival at Kempton three weeks ago and moves into handicaps with some potential.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Closely matched with Alasrae on C&D form from Good Friday and his effort there can be marked up given he was poorly drawn; can be given a pass for Bath last time (hampered) and he has yet to run a poor race over C&D; more exposed than some but still commands respect.
horses.breeding: b g Mohaather - Today's The Day

horses.spotlight_comment: He has won three of his last four starts (good second on the other occasion) yet has only gone up 8lb; finished with a flourish to win over C&D on Good Friday and he is a leading contender despite his wide draw.
horses.breeding: gr g Havana Grey - Up To Speed

horses.spotlight_comment: 2-2 on AW, the wins coming on his racecourse debut (5f) and then after a three-month break in November (7f; tongue tied first time); given that ability fresh a 171-day absence is of little concern but a 5lb rise for beating a small field when last seen isn't obviously generous; stable also represented by Eternal Solace.

He has finished third in each of his novice/maiden runs, with the first and third coming over today's C&D; cheekpieces which debuted last time are retained; makes his handicap debut with his trainer banging in the winners.
horses.breeding: b c No Nay Never - Marsh Hawk

horses.spotlight_comment: C&D winner as a 2yo; two promising efforts this year, shaping nicely at Kempton before chasing home her hugely progressive stablemate Al Najashi at Newcastle on Good Friday; hit with a 3lb rise but she is still a key player now back down in class; stable also run Bone Marra.
6f turf win last May; back at that level when a close third of eight in a 6f handicap at Kempton three weeks ago; races off the same mark and should make another bold bid.
horses.breeding: b g Dark Angel - Thread Of Silver

horses.spotlight_comment: All runs at 5f; won a Wolverhampton fillies' maiden last June on her second start; good second at Nottingham one month later but she has found it much harder work since, most recently finishing last of eight at Wolverhampton four weeks ago; others appeal more.
horses.breeding: b f Due Diligence - Jungle Boogaloo

horses.spotlight_comment: Well beaten on his debut (6.5f, good) but he has run well in three AW maidens since; moves into handicaps with the potential for rmore but he will need to step forward to defy this mark.
Promising start to his career, albeit in weak small-field AW events, before a hefty defeat at Thirsk on his handicap debut ten days ago; return to AW can help but not sure he's well treated.
Always behind after an awkward start at Wolverhampton last month; even her peak 2yo efforts, which included two wins, need bettering if she is to take this.
horses.breeding: b f Dandy Man - Law Keeper

horses.spotlight_comment: Ran out the ready winner of a 6f novice on his racecourse debut last summer; disappointed at Thirsk one month later but he was back on the up with a good second at Kempton on his return three weeks ago (conceding 5lb to a promising winner); remains capable of better and he is well drawn to attack; respected.
horses.breeding: b g Kodi Bear - Harlequin Twist

6.20.betting_forecast: 2/1 Enter Sandman, 3/1 Luna Beaux, 6/1 No Claims Bonus, 8/1 Mortubo, Saddle Up, 12/1 Power Cut, 16/1 Dusk Damsel, Sun
6.20.spotlight_verdict: A 6lb penalty for Enter Sandman's hard-fought success at Newcastle last week could leave him vulnerable. There are some interesting handicap newcomers for whom the market needs a close look but the two to appeal most are Luna Beaux, who could resume her progress back at 6f, and NO CLAIMS BONUS. The selection would have finished a good deal closer at Nottingham on her reappearance had she seen any daylight and Billy Loughnane is a notable booking.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Good run when second at Chelmsford on his nursery debut in December (5f; cheekpieces first time); struggled since and hopes rest on the new tongue tie giving him a lift.
horses.breeding: b g Soldier's Call - Tartufo Dolce

horses.spotlight_comment: Poor form in four runs for Archie Watson last year; the new hood needs to make a big difference on her seasonal and stable debut.
horses.breeding: b f Due Diligence - David's Duchess

horses.spotlight_comment: She hinted at ability in three maiden runs over further last month; improvement possible dropping to 6f for her handicap debut but the handicapper has taken no chances.

He had been threatening a bigger effort prior to last week's breakthrough success at Newcastle (5f), a race where he dug deep to scramble home in a blanket finish (0.75l split the first five home); not well in under a penalty but in form and stepping back up to 6f should be fine.
The winner of two of her five starts for her new stable, both over 6f at Wolverhampton; found out by the drop to 5f at Bath three weeks ago; could resume her progress back at 6f.
horses.breeding: b f Saxon Warrior - The Stalking Moon

horses.spotlight_comment: Unplaced in three runs in the second half of 2025, recording her best RPR over C&D when last seen 196 days ago; may do better this year but would want to see market support before getting involved.

Yet to kick on from her Wolverhampton third last September (5f) but she wasn't able to show what she could do at Nottingham on her recent return, having nowhere to go as the race was unfolding; steps up to 6f and remains capable of better.

Down the field in three novice/maiden runs on AW since October; charted a wide course and still looked green at Wolverhampton when last seen eight weeks ago; open to improvement in handicaps but he is drawn widest this time; betting to guide.
Low-level form in three AW maiden/novice runs this year; bred to do much better at some point but he looks the stable second string today.
Poor form in three 6f novice events at Kempton; bred to do a fair bit better at some point.

6.50.betting_forecast: 11/10 Knights Charge, 7/4 Cyrano De Bergerac, 8/1 Mr Bollinger, 10/1 Be Hopeful, 12/1 Leonato, 14/1 Liveinthelight, 50/1
6.50.spotlight_verdict: Lots depends on the level of market confidence behind the Palace Pier colt Cyrano De Bergerac who could be a cut above these. However, KNIGHTS CHARGE has the benefit of experience and it was a nice run at Kempton last year. The now-gelded Leonato is expected to perform much better than on his debut.[Alistair Jones]

horses.spotlight_comment: 95,000euros foal; brother to 7f 2yo winner Bold Impact (RPR 87) and half-brother to winners Keeper Of Time (6f-1m; Group 3; 101) and Maggie's Delight (2m1f; 85); dam Italian Listed-placed 5.5f-1m winner; gelded ahead of debut; market can guide.
Tailed off on three visits to Kempton, over 1m, 7f and 1m3f; no appeal.
horses.breeding: b f Flag Of Honour - Outshine

horses.spotlight_comment: By the stable's star miler Palace Pier and this colt cost 150,000gns as a yearling; second foal; dam 1m4f AW winner (RPR 78); kicks off in a modest race and would be hard to resist if at all strong in the betting.
100,000euros yearling who is related to winners from 5f to 1m5f; the penny dropped late on at Kempton in December (1m; 10-1) when he was doing his best work late on; should be very competitive.
Half-brother to French/Australian 1m1f-1m2f winner Barazin; very green when beaten 20l at Newcastle in November (1m; 11-2) and could easily leave that form behind now gelded; market informative.
290,000gns yearling; showed more on her reappearance when fifth of eight at Kempton (1m3f) but she posted a modest RPR; remains best watched.
Hurdle/chase winner who has offered very little in his two runs on the Flat.
40-1 and was beaten a shade under 10l at Nottingham three weeks ago (1m2f); could be one for further down the line.
2,000gns 2yo; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Ski Lift (1m1f/1m2f) and Try Out (1m4f); can only be watched on this belated debut.

7.20.betting_forecast: 7/2 Penfolds Grange, 4/1 Criminal, Lenny's Spirit, 6/1 Joseph, 7/1 Romantic Spirit, 9/1 Etretat, 14/1 Onslow Gardens, 16/1 Voix
7.20.spotlight_verdict: Joseph, Penfolds Grange, Etretat and Lenny's Spirit (second choice) all have something to recommend them but this could be the day for CRIMINAL to shed his maiden tag. Although his never-dangerous eighth over 1m here two weeks ago doesn't read especially well, he had no chance the way things panned out and he was finishing on the front foot. Dropping in class and stepping back up in trip could be the catalyst for a full revival.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Recorded RPRs of 70 (twice) and 75 in her three novice/maiden runs last season; struggled badly in four handicap runs thereafter, dropping 9lb in the process; may bounce back at some point but she is risky back from a 202-day break.
horses.breeding: b f Blue Point - Norway Cross

horses.spotlight_comment: Ten-race maiden and out of sorts so far this year; had little chance the way the race panned out in a 1m handicap here two weeks ago but he was keeping on well at the finish, boding well for today's return to 1m2f; drops in class too and he's of interest.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Moon - Alea Iacta

horses.spotlight_comment: Four AW wins, including C&D, and returns from a six-month break on a manageable mark; more good runs than bad at this track and he's not discounted.

Formerly trained by Adam West; two wins over 8.5f at Epsom in 2024; several good runs in France last year, including a 9.5f AW win at Chantilly; starts out for Jim Boyle on a feasible mark but he is eligible for weaker races than this one; absent 284 days.
horses.breeding: b g Charm Spirit - World Class

horses.spotlight_comment: Off the mark at the 16th attempt when overcoming adversity to win a C&D handicap in February; similar form when second at Kempton last month and subsequent turf flop easy enough to forgive (yet to show anything on grass); better expected back on AW and with Billy Loughnane booked.
horses.breeding: ch g Earthlight - Take A Deep Breath

horses.spotlight_comment: Just 1-28 on AW but he went desperately close to doubling that tally in an amateur rider's race over C&D last month, only headed in the dying strides (first run for Adam Kirby); 2lb higher today; one to consider with new headgear tried.

19-race maiden; ran some good races in defeat for this yard last year, including when last seen in October (1m2f, good to soft); withdrawn at the start having got upset in the stalls ahead of this month's intended return (10-1 at the time of withdrawal); others preferred for win purposes.
Had wind surgery in December and he has run three good races since, finishing fourth over C&D before two runner-up efforts at Kempton (1m); should remain competitive.
horses.breeding: b g Time Test - Posh Claret

horses.spotlight_comment: 4-11 on AW and only 1lb higher than for last October's front-running win at Southwell (1m3f); lower draw would have been ideal but she has the ability to feature.
Well beaten over hurdles three weeks ago and that followed a disappointing run at Kempton; his earlier AW form brings him into the reckoning but that was over further; others appeal more.

7.50.betting_forecast: 4/9 Wild Thoughts, 13/2 Timely Salute, 7/1 Katalyst, Labiche, 12/1 Bennyworth, 33/1 Betty Lemon.
7.50.spotlight_verdict: This is a quick return for WILD THOUGHTS following his barnstorming win at Redcar last week but it's still hard to make a case for any of his rivals. Best of them may be Timely Salute but Labiche was never likely to show much as a 2yo and he could be a big improver this year.[Emily Weber]

horses.spotlight_comment: Ran well for a long way on second and final start for James Owen (6f, AW) but always behind over C&D on yard debut; gelded since; handicaps should offer more scope but his opening mark doesn't look overly generous.
Minor 2yo form, finding nothing new when switched to handicaps (1m; turf and AW) in the autumn and has plenty to find on her return; hood added.
horses.breeding: gr f Land Force - Tremelo Pointe

horses.spotlight_comment: Best efforts over 7f elsewhere but she didn't look as if the 1m trip was beyond her when fifth of nine on handicap debut at Southwell in December; overall form suggests improvement needed for the return to Polytrack.

Late foal who hinted at some ability over 7f and 1m last summer; gelded since; has been off since August but he's well connected and may well show more now handicapping for a yard among the winners of late.

Fair 7f debut on Chelmsford AW but never involved in two 1m starts after, most recently in a Yarmouth novice 17 days ago; his pedigree suggests that trips beyond 1m may be ideal but still a likely type for handicaps and the betting can guide.

Some sprint promise in early 2025; pedigree promised improvement for 1m on handicap debut at Redcar (good to firm) last week and it came to pass in some style; makes a quick return under a penalty but likely still well in; big chance on AW debut.
horses.breeding: b g Lucky Vega - She's Complete
